title: RoboHack AI CTF (Robotic Hacking Community at DEFCON 34)
description:
RoboHack AI CTF is an experimental Capture The Flag event hosted by the Robotic Hacking Community at DEF CON 34.
The CTF target will be an AI robot inside a simulated environment. Instead of requiring continuous manual player interaction, the competition may allow participants to submit their own AI models or agents, which will then be used to interact with, exploit, or solve challenges against the robotic target environment.
The challenge scope may include both AI model security and robotics system security. In addition to allowing participants to compete using AI models, the target systems and challenges themselves may involve AI models such as VLA, VLM, or LLM components. Potential challenge topics may include adversarial patches, prompt injection, prompt jailbreaks, model poisoning, and other attacks against AI-enabled robotic decision-making systems.
The CTF may also include challenges related to the robot’s underlying software stack, communication layers, and robotics protocols, such as ROS 2, DDS, and related robotic middleware or system interfaces.
The goal is to explore the intersection of robotics security, AI model behavior, autonomous exploitation, and CTF-style challenge design. Participants may be asked to think beyond traditional web, pwn, reversing, or cloud challenges and consider how autonomous systems perceive, decide, communicate, and act inside a robotic environment.
This event is expected to be experimental and community-driven. Details such as rules, scoring, participation format, model submission requirements, challenge categories, target environments, and challenge availability may change as the event develops.
Please refer to the official Robotic Hacking Community website for the latest and most accurate event information.
Tentative Challenge Areas
AI robotic security
Autonomous agent / AI model participation
VLA, VLM, and LLM security
Adversarial patch attacks
Prompt injection
Prompt jailbreak
Model poisoning
AI-enabled robotic decision-making
ROS 2 / DDS security
Robotic middleware and communication protocols
Simulated robotic target environments

title: THJCC CTF 2026 summer
description:
THJCC CTF is a cybersecurity competition tailored specifically for high school and vocational school students in Taiwan. It is co-hosted by the SCINT (Northern Taiwan Student Information Community) and like-minded students nationwide, and has received the support of multiple domestic cybersecurity organizations and institutions. Continuing the tradition of previous events, we are specially hosting the THJCC CTF 3rd Summer Edition this summer, hoping to bring students a cybersecurity feast full of challenges and fun during their vacation. This competition maintains the Jeopardy format, with challenges covering Web, Reverse, Crypto, Pwn, and Misc. The difficulty level balances introductory learning for novices and advanced challenges, ensuring that everyone—from beginners just starting in cybersecurity to experienced competitors—can find an opportunity to showcase their skills here. Our core mission is to promote cybersecurity education and cultivate high school students' keen interest and practical abilities in cybersecurity technology. Beyond the competition, participants in the student division have the opportunity to win prize money or other special rewards, with the hope of boosting their confidence in tackling various future competitions. THJCC CTF is not merely a stage for competition, but also a platform for students across Taiwan to learn from each other, hone their skills, and exchange ideas.

title: Haruulzangi CTF 2026 Qualifier
description:
Haruul Zangi CTF 2026 is organized by MNCERT/CC and the Haruulzangi CTF Team, representing the Mongolian CERT and cybersecurity community.
We are proud to announce the 14th edition of Haruul Zangi CTF and welcome participants from around the world. The competition aims to promote practical cybersecurity skills, encourage knowledge sharing, and strengthen collaboration within the global cybersecurity community.

Competition Format
The competition consists of three rounds:
Round 1 – Qualification (Online, Jeopardy)
•	Date: August 22, 2026 
•	Start Time: 09:00 (UTC+8) 
•	Duration: 24 hours 
Round 2 – Semi-Final (Onsite, Jeopardy)
•	Date: September 5, 2026 
•	Location: Mongolia 
Round 3 – Final (Onsite, Attack & Defense)
•	Date: September 24, 2026 
•	Location: Mongolia 

Challenge Categories
•	Pwn 
•	Web 
•	Forensics 
•	Cryptography 
•	Reverse Engineering 
•	Miscellaneous 
The challenges range from beginner to advanced difficulty, providing an engaging experience for both new and experienced CTF players.

Team Information
•	Teams may consist of up to 3 players. 
•	International participants are welcome. 

Qualification
The following teams will advance to the onsite Semi-Final:
•	The top 30 teams from the online Qualification Round. 
•	The top high school team (if not already qualified through the overall ranking). 
•	The top women's team (if not already qualified through the overall ranking). 
The Semi-Final will be held in Jeopardy format. At the end of the Semi-Final, the top 10 teams will qualify for the onsite Final, which will be played in the Attack & Defense format.
Additionally, two international teams will be invited directly to participate in the onsite Final.

Support for International Finalists
The organizers will provide the following support for the two invited international finalist teams:
•	Hotel accommodation during the onsite event. 
•	A daily allowance to cover meals and local expenses. 
Invited international teams are responsible for:
•	International and domestic transportation. 
•	Airfare and all other travel-related expenses. 
Visa invitation letters and supporting documents will be provided upon request.

Previous Challenges
Challenges from previous Haruul Zangi CTF competitions are publicly available in our GitHub organization:
https://github.com/haruulzangi
We look forward to welcoming teams from Mongolia and around the world to Haruul Zangi CTF 2026.
Good luck, have fun, and see you in Mongolia!

title: PINK+ CTF 2026
description:
The first iteration of PINK+ CTF. Explore a variety of hand crafted challenges with a focus on steganography!

Discord: https://discord.gg/VuPqnhFxH4

title: CSCTF 2026
description:
"CSCTF 2026: Total Warfare" is an international, online, free jeopardy-style CTF focused on realistic cybersecurity scenarios inspired by critical infrastructure, defense, and modern adversary tactics.

Challenges cover web, pwn, crypto, reverse engineering, forensics, misc, Linux, Windows, and operational security, with scenarios connected to energy, telecom, healthcare, finance, and defense environments.

The competition is somewhat beginner-friendly but realism-driven.

title: WolvCTF 2026
description:
Our challenges range from beginner to hard in difficulty. Our esteemed members have worked tirelessly to bring new and stimulating CTF challenges to pose varying levels of difficulty and topic (RE, binary exploit, web exploit, cryptography, forensics, osint, misc.). 

There are two divisions, Open and University of Michigan students. No team limit sizes.

Sponsors to be announced!

**Note: This event has been postponed to November 2026**

title: Platypwn 2026
description:
The Platypwn 2026 is an online Jeopardy CTF which offers easy challenges for beginners, but also medium and difficult challenges for advanced players.

See https://platypwnies.de/events/platypwn for further details.

title: GlacierCTF 2026
description:
We're excited to announce GlacierCTF 2026 for its fifth edition, a 24-hour jeopardy CTF organized by LosFuzzys.

Join our discord at:
https://discord.gg/DFYnRAME23

Infra sponsored by goo.gle/ctfsponsorship

title: SwampCTF 2026
description: SwampCTF is a student-run competition and hosted by the University of Florida Student InfoSec Team (UFSIT). Join us online for jeopardy-style fun with challenges in Pwn, Reverse, Forensics, Crypto, and Misc. categories.

title: niteCTF 2026
description: niteCTF, hosted by Cryptonite, is designed to help students explore new & diverse areas of cybersecurity while providing a platform for experienced players to sharpen their skills. The CTF features a wide range of challenges spanning multiple domains including hardware security, cryptography, web exploitation, digital forensics, binary exploitation, reverse engineering, and more!
